sections.heading: Greece Cruise Packages & Greek Island Cruises 2026–2027

blocks.text: See the Greek islands from the water with Greece cruise packages that sail through the Aegean and connect Athens with some of Greece’s best-known islands. Choose a multi-day Greek island cruise or combine your sailing with extra nights on land for more time in Athens and selected destinations.

See mainland Greece without having to plan every connection yourself. Our Greece escorted tours bring together guided sightseeing, transportation, and some of the country’s most important historical sites, with routes through Athens, Delphi, Meteora, and the Peloponnese. Selected journeys can also continue to the Greek islands.

Staying in Athens doesn’t mean spending every day in the city. Our Greece day tours take you to places such as Delphi, Cape Sounion, Corinth, Mycenae, Epidaurus, and the Saronic Islands, with half-day and full-day options that bring you back without adding another overnight stop.

Greece is one of those countries where the route matters as much as the number of days you have. You might spend a few days in Athens before heading to Santorini and Mykonos, stay longer on one island, or keep more of the trip on the mainland with Delphi and Meteora.

Our Greece Tours generally run from 6 to 15 days, with different ways to put the trip together. Some itineraries are private and flexible, others follow a more structured escorted program, and there are also cruise-based options. Depending on the tour, arrangements can include selected hotels, ferries or domestic flights, airport and port transfers, and guided sightseeing. Customized Tours are also available when an existing itinerary is close to what you want but needs a few changes.

Greece has 19 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, but a trip here does not have to be built entirely around sightseeing. Athens and the mainland offer plenty of history, while the islands give you time to slow down, spend a few days by the sea, and experience a very different side of the country.

Athens is usually the easiest place to start. The Acropolis, Parthenon, Acropolis Museum, and Ancient Agora cover much of the city's classical history, while Plaka and Monastiraki are better explored without much of a plan. Two or three nights gives most first-time visitors enough time before continuing to the islands or mainland.

Santorini is small enough to explore without filling every day with activities. Oia and Fira are the best-known towns, but there are also volcanic beaches, wineries, archaeological sites, and villages away from the busiest viewpoints. Most of our itineraries leave enough free time here rather than turning the whole stay into organized sightseeing.

Mykonos has a different feel again. Beaches are a big part of the island, but Mykonos Town, Little Venice, and the windmills are all worth seeing on foot. If ancient history is still on your list after Athens, nearby Delos can be visited as a day trip.

Meteora is on the mainland, well away from the island routes. Its monasteries sit on huge natural rock formations above the town of Kalambaka, and the setting is unlike anywhere else in Greece. It is often paired with Delphi as part of a longer mainland itinerary.

Delphi can be visited from Athens or included on the way north toward Meteora. The archaeological site includes the Temple of Apollo and ancient theatre, with the mountains around the sanctuary forming an important part of the setting.

sections.heading: Athens, the Islands or the Mainland?

blocks.text: For a first visit, Athens plus Santorini or Mykonos is an easy place to start. With more time, you can add a second island or spend part of the trip on the mainland rather than moving from island to island.

Our Greece Travel Packages cover flexible multi-day itineraries, while Greece Cruise Packages are better suited to travelers who prefer to see several islands without changing hotels each time. For a more structured program, see our Greece Escorted Tours.
April through October covers the main travel season, but the experience changes considerably between spring, midsummer, and early autumn.

May, June, September, and early October work particularly well if you want to combine sightseeing with the islands. July and August bring hotter weather and busier resorts, but also the widest choice of ferry connections and a livelier atmosphere on islands such as Mykonos.

How much moving around you want to do is worth deciding early. Visiting Athens, Santorini, Mykonos, Crete, Delphi, and Meteora in the same trip may look appealing on a map, but adding another destination is not always the best use of an extra day.

Private Tours offer more flexibility with sightseeing and timing, while escorted programs follow a more established schedule. If you prefer something in between, we can adjust many of our Greece itineraries around your dates, hotel preferences, and the amount of free time you want.
Greece can also be part of a longer regional trip. See our Turkey & Greece Vacation Packages, Greece & Egypt Holidays, or Greece & Jordan Tours if you are considering more than one country.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for a Greece tour?
faqs.a: Most travelers spend 7 to 10 days exploring Greece. This allows enough time to visit Athens, Santorini, and Mykonos while enjoying both guided sightseeing and leisure time. If you would like to include Crete, Meteora, or Delphi, we recommend extending your trip to 10–15 days for a more complete experience.

faqs.q: What is the best Greece itinerary for first-time visitors?
faqs.a: An 8 to 10-day itinerary is ideal for first-time visitors. Most travelers begin in Athens to explore ancient landmarks before continuing to Santorini and Mykonos. This combination offers an excellent balance of history, island scenery, local culture, and relaxation while covering Greece's most iconic destinations.

faqs.q: What is included in your Greece Tour Packages?
faqs.a: Our Greece Tour Packages typically include carefully selected hotels, daily breakfast, airport transfers, domestic flights or ferry tickets where applicable, licensed local guides, sightseeing tours, and transportation during guided excursions. Individual itineraries may vary depending on the tour duration, destination, and level of customization selected.

faqs.q: Do you offer both Private Tours and Small Group Tours?
faqs.a: Yes. We offer Private Tours, Small Group Tours, and fully Customized Tours throughout Greece. Private tours provide complete flexibility, personalized sightseeing, and private transportation, while small group tours offer excellent value and the opportunity to travel with like-minded visitors in professionally organized groups.

faqs.q: Can I customize my Greece itinerary?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Every itinerary can be customized to match your travel style, available time, accommodation preferences, sightseeing priorities, and budget. You may add extra nights, visit additional islands, upgrade hotels, combine destinations, or create a completely personalized itinerary designed by our experienced travel consultants.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Greece?
faqs.a: The best time to visit Greece is generally between April and June or September and October. These months offer pleasant temperatures, fewer crowds, and ideal sightseeing conditions. July and August are perfect for beach holidays and island vacations but are also the busiest and warmest months.

faqs.q: Which Greek islands are best to visit?
faqs.a: Santorini and Mykonos are Greece's most popular islands, especially for first-time visitors. Crete offers beautiful beaches, historical sites, and traditional villages, while Rhodes combines medieval history with coastal scenery. The best choice depends on your interests, travel style, and the amount of time available.

faqs.q: Should I visit Santorini or Mykonos?
faqs.a: Both islands offer unique experiences. Santorini is famous for its volcanic caldera, dramatic sunsets, luxury hotels, and romantic atmosphere, making it ideal for couples and honeymooners. Mykonos is known for beautiful beaches, waterfront restaurants, lively nightlife, and charming whitewashed streets suitable for all types of travelers.

faqs.q: Is it better to travel between the islands by ferry or flight?
faqs.a: Both options are available depending on your itinerary. Ferries offer a scenic and authentic island-hopping experience, while domestic flights save valuable travel time on longer routes. Our destination specialists recommend the most practical combination based on your selected destinations and travel schedule.

faqs.q: Are ferry tickets included in your tours?
faqs.a: Yes. Whenever ferry transportation forms part of your itinerary, all required ferry tickets are arranged in advance and included according to your package. We carefully coordinate ferry schedules with hotel stays, airport transfers, and sightseeing to ensure a smooth and stress-free travel experience.

faqs.q: Do I need a visa to visit Greece?
faqs.a: Visa requirements depend on your nationality. Greece is part of the Schengen Area, and many travelers can enter visa-free for short tourist stays. If a visa is required, we recommend applying well before departure. Our travel consultants can provide general guidance before you finalize your booking.

faqs.q: Are Greece tours suitable for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes. Greece is an excellent destination for families thanks to its safe environment, welcoming atmosphere, beautiful beaches, fascinating historical attractions, and family-friendly accommodations. We can customize itineraries with shorter travel times, child-friendly activities, and hotels that best suit families traveling with children.

faqs.q: Are your Greece tours suitable for honeymoon couples?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Greece is one of Europe's most romantic destinations. Honeymoon itineraries often include Santorini, Mykonos, or Crete with luxury hotels, private transfers, sunset cruises, and optional upgrades designed to create a memorable and relaxing travel experience tailored to each couple.

Yes. All guided sightseeing is conducted by experienced, licensed local guides who possess extensive knowledge of Greek history, archaeology, culture, and local traditions. Their expertise provides valuable insight into each destination while ensuring an informative, engaging, and professionally organized touring experience.

faqs.q: Why book your Greece Tour Packages with Magnificent Travel?
faqs.a: Since 1997, Magnificent Travel has specialized in professionally organized travel experiences across Greece and the Eastern Mediterranean. Our experienced destination specialists provide carefully planned itineraries, transparent pricing, handpicked hotels, licensed local guides, reliable transportation, and personalized support before and throughout your journey, ensuring a seamless and memorable vacation.
